newsitem.title: USA: HFS, Leon Black's Apollo form $232 million venture.
newsitem.headline: HFS, Leon Black's Apollo form $232 million venture.

text.p: HFS Inc., a real estate and travel services company, and a group affiliated with investor Leon Black's Apollo Management LP, said Tuesday they formed a $232 million venture to acquire real estate brokerage firms.

HFS and the Apollo group also said that the new venture, NRT Inc., has agreed to acquire the assets of National Realty Trust, the nation's largest residential real estate brokerage and HFS' largest real estate franchisee.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
National Realty Trust owns and operates 400 residential realty offices under HFS' Century 21, Coldwell Banker and ERA franchise systems. National Realty Trust's sales were about $700 million in 1996.
"The real estate brokerage industry is extremely fragmented and represents a huge opportunity for consolidation," HRS Chairman Henry Silverman said in a statement.
"We expect that NRT will complete substantial acquisition activity by the end of 1997, and anticipate an expansion of its activities thereafter."
Of NRT's initial $232 million in funding, HFS will invest $157 million. Apollo, an investment firm founded by Black, who is well known on Wall Street, and other institutions will invest $75 million.
When those transactions are completed, NRT together with other assets will have about $575 million in cash and other funds for acquisitions.

NRT also has reached agreements with several other large real estate brokerages for other acquisitions. The deals, whose terms were not disclosed, are subject to reaching definitive agreements and other conditions, the groups said.
They said NRT will use its capital mainly to acquire residential real estate brokerage offices not affiliated with HFS and convert them to HFS franchises.
In addition, they said NRT will use PHH Mortgage Services, a unit of HFS, to be the sole mortgage lender in NRT offices.
NRT expects to complete the purchase of National Realty Trust by the end of August.
HFS stock rose 87.5 cents to $63.44 in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
